answer: Yes. A meteg is printed under the lamed (ל), the first lamed in the word, which carries a tsere. Reading: עָלֵֽינוּ. Host letter: lamed, certain. Host vowel: tsere, certain.
visible_evidence: The image shows the whole word עלינו with all of its lower points; the cropped snippet contains only this one occurrence. Under the ayin is a qamats: a horizontal bar with a short vertical stem, drawn as part of the same mark. Under the lamed are two dots side by side, which is a tsere. Just to the left of the tsere, toward the yod, is a separate short vertical stroke. It is clearly apart from the qamats stem and lines up with the tsere, so it is a meteg on the lamed. No mark appears under the yod. There is a dot (shuruk) in the vav. Ink from the line below is visible at the bottom edge but well below the lower points, so it does not touch the vowel area.
